entities.summary: Marcus Simplicinius Genialis was a Roman governor and military leader who played a crucial role in maintaining Roman power in the region of Illyricum during the late 3rd century CE. As the Roman governor of Illyricum, he oversaw the construction of the city of Salona, which became a major center of Roman culture and trade. His military campaigns against the Goths and other barbarian tribes helped to secure the borders of the Roman Empire. Despite his significant contributions to Roman power, Genialis's life remains somewhat of a mystery, and his exact dates of birth and death are unknown. However, his legacy can be seen in the continued influence of Roman culture and architecture in the region, which has endured for centuries. The inscription on the tomb of a Roman officer at Salona, which reads 'Genialis, governor of Illyricum', provides a tangible link to his life and career. The fact that Genialis was able to maintain Roman power in Illyricum despite the significant challenges posed by the barbarian tribes is a testament to his skill and strategic thinking. His military campaigns also had a profound impact on the development of the region, shaping the course of local history and influencing the eventual rise of the Byzantine Empire.
